title: Onboarding Cost Guardrails & Developer Debt Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the product and operational approach for protecting both Redwood and our developer customers from runaway consumption during developer onboarding and early-stage experiments. It combines UX guardrails, automated cost signals, and short-term crediting mechanics to reduce customer surprise, prevent billing disputes, and limit developer friction.

Context and problem statement:
- New developers frequently create unrestricted routes, long prompt experiments, or embed heavy-batch workloads during trial periods which can generate outsized token spend and lead to negative CX and increased support load.
- Product teams need a low-friction way to let developers explore capabilities while enforcing predictable unit economics.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce onboarding-related inflated spend by >= 65% for new accounts in the first 14 days.
- Decrease billing dispute incidence from onboarding traffic by 50% within the first three months of rollout.
- Preserve exploratory developer experience: no more than 10% drop in successful sign-up-to-API-call conversion.
- Provide transparent, actionable signals in the Console and API for both customers and internal teams.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for enterprise negotiated contracts or long-term dedicated capacity commitment flows.
- It does not modify existing SLA definitions for committed customers.

Key concepts and primitives:
- Consumption Guardrails: a set of tiered default limits applied to new accounts and routes (tokens-per-minute, tokens-per-request, concurrent-streams).
- Developer Credit Watch: short-lived credits that can be automatically applied and revoked based on behavioral signals (e.g., spike detection, repeated over-budget calls).
- Soft Fidelity Negotiation: lightweight automatic fallback of high-cost model variants to lower-cost compatible variants during onboarding experiments with customer-visible annotations.
- Audit-first Visibility: enriched Console pages and billing export that attribute onboarding spend to route/prompt-set and includes recommended mitigations.

High-level product behavior:
1) At account creation the platform attaches a default onboarding profile for 14 days: tokens/min cap = 150k, tokens/request cap = 25k, concurrent-streams = 3.
2) The Onboarding Advisor surfaces explainers and quick toggles in the Console ("Increase temporarily", "Request review", "Enable credit watch").
3) When the credit watch triggers (see thresholds below), the crediting-engine applies a short-term credit cap and sends structured notifications to both Console and email; optionally creates a support ticket for accounts that are flagged as high-risk.
4) Soft fidelity negotiation can replace a high-cost variant (e.g., full-precision large model) with a quantized, validated fallback variant if the request matches a heuristic pattern (long context + few tokens expected). The response includes a metadata field: fallback_reason and estimated cost delta.

Configuration matrix (reference defaults):
| Profile | Duration | tokens/min | tokens/request | concurrent-streams | credit-watch-threshold | initial-credit |
| Default Onboarding | 14d | 150000 | 25000 | 3 | 2x daily baseline spike OR > $50 over expected trial | $50 |
| Extended Trial (sales-enabled) | 30d | 300000 | 50k | 6 | 1.5x baseline OR > $200 | $250 |
| Sandbox (dev-only) | unlimited | 50k | 5k | 2 | manual enable | $0 |

Implementation requirements (product + engineering):
- API: new account profile endpoint. Fields: profile_type, duration_days, tokens_per_min, tokens_per_request, concurrency_limit, enable_credit_watch (boolean). Example request: 
  POST /v1/accounts/{id}/onboarding-profile 
  { "profile_type": "default_onboarding", "duration_days": 14, "tokens_per_min": 150000 }
- Console: onboarding card visible during initial 14 days with clear spend estimation and one-click actions.
- Telemetry: synthetic metric onboarding.tokens_spend_by_route.dimension(route, model_variant, time_window) emitted at 1m cadence.
- Crediting-engine: transactional audit log for credits applied/removed; idempotent operations and TTLs for short-lived credits.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Canary (2 weeks) - opt-in for 5% of new signups. Metrics: signup->first-call conversion, onboarding spend per account. Owner: Growth + Product.
2) Gradual enable (6 weeks) - increase to 50% with telemetry instrumentation and support training. Add automated emails.
3) Global default (2 weeks) - flip default for all new accounts; begin retroactive analysis for 30-day adoption.
4) Enterprise opt-out path - provide admin API to disable or customize profile for negotiated customers. Requirement: enterprise admin audit and RBAC check.

Numbered operational playbook (support + SRE):
1. Alert: onboarding-spend-rate > 90th percentile and credit-watch triggered -> Pager to CostOps channel (P2).
2. Triage: check Console onboarding card and crediting-engine audit log. Document route IDs and user actions.
3. Mitigation: temporarily escalate credit limit or pause the offending route using admin console, notify customer via templated email.
4. Post-incident: create retro in CostOps; apply product change if pattern repeats more than 3 times in 14 days for same account.

SLOs & success metrics:
- Onboarding spend reduction target: 65% reduction in median 14-day onboarding spend (measured vs baseline cohort).
- Billing dispute reduction: reduce disputes connected to onboarding traffic by 50% in 90 days.
- Console visibility SLA: onboarding advisor page loads within 200ms P95; telemetry uplink delay <= 60s P95.

Pricing & packaging implications:
- Short-lived credits are accounted as promotional credits in billing; Finance will treat applied credits as contra-revenue. Policy: credits > $1k per account must be approved by Sales.
- The product must surface predicted monthly run-rate impact if the global default is applied to existing paying customers (risk analysis required before global flips).

User-facing messaging and UX guidelines:
- Be explicit: show estimated cost impact for toggles (e.g., increase tokens/request -> +$X/day at current usage).
- Offer a one-click explanation: "Why was my call throttled?" with automated remediation steps.
- Provide an in-console "appeal" flow that generates a support ticket with pre-filled telemetry.

Security & compliance notes:
- Crediting operations are sensitive: require audit logging, RBAC checks and immutability for at least 90 days.
- For private (VPC/on-prem) customers the guardrails are advisory by default and must be deployable via customer-managed config.

Ownership and next steps:
- Product: Maya Chen (owner), Arjun Patel (stakeholder), Customer Success for playbook templates.
- Engineering: Crediting-engine team for implementation; Onboarding-advisor UI ownership with Console team.
- Finance: finalize credit accounting rules and thresholds by 2026-07-10.

Appendix - sample customer-facing copy (Console):
- Heading: "Onboarding protections are active"
- Body: "To prevent unexpected charges while you evaluate Redwood, we apply temporary rate limits and small credits. You can request a temporary increase or ask for a review."

Appendix - example profile YAML (for internal ops):
profile: default_onboarding
duration_days: 14
tokens_per_min: 150000
tokens_per_request: 25000
concurrency: 3
enable_credit_watch: true
initial_credit_cents: 5000

slo_summary: Console load P95 <= 200ms; telemetry uplink <= 60s P95; onboarding spend reduction >= 65% in 14-day window
